text.tspan: Same matrix: R ← D, V ← I. Now every pivot is applied immediately to all columns to its right,
so each column is already fully reduced when reached. Green: pivot column and row. Orange: columns it is applied to.
Column 1: pivot low(1) = 5. Look ahead along row 5: columns 3, 6 have an entry there.
Apply the pivot column (green) to each of them (orange), in R and in V — whether or not their own pivots collide.
Row 5 is now zero to the right of its pivot (dark gray = changed entries).
Column 2: pivot low(2) = 2. Look ahead along row 2: columns 3, 4, 7 have an entry there.
Apply the pivot column (green) to each of them (orange), in R and in V — whether or not their own pivots collide.
Row 2 is now zero to the right of its pivot (dark gray = changed entries).
Column 3 = {1, 4, 6, 8} Column 4 = {1, 3, 4} Column 7 = {7}
Column 3: pivot low(3) = 8. Look ahead along row 8: column 8 has an entry there.
Apply the pivot column (green) to each of them (orange), in R and in V — whether or not their own pivots collide.
Row 8 is now zero to the right of its pivot (dark gray = changed entries).
Column 8 = {1, 6}
Column 4: pivot low(4) = 4. Look ahead along row 4: columns 5, 6 have an entry there.
Apply the pivot column (green) to each of them (orange), in R and in V — whether or not their own pivots collide.
Row 4 is now zero to the right of its pivot (dark gray = changed entries).
Column 5 = {3} Column 6 = {3, 7}
Column 5: pivot low(5) = 3. Look ahead along row 3: column 6 has an entry there.
Apply the pivot column (green) to each of them (orange), in R and in V — whether or not their own pivots collide.
Row 3 is now zero to the right of its pivot (dark gray = changed entries).
Column 6 = {7}
Column 6: pivot low(6) = 7. Look ahead along row 7: column 7 has an entry there.
Apply the pivot column (green) to each of them (orange), in R and in V — whether or not their own pivots collide.
Row 7 is now zero to the right of its pivot (dark gray = changed entries).
Column 7 = 0
Column 7 is zero when reached: no pivot, nothing to apply (a "positive" column).
Column 8: pivot low(8) = 6. Row 6 is already zero to the right: nothing to do.
Done. Same pivots as the lazy reduction: (5, 1), (2, 2), (8, 3), (4, 4), (3, 5), (7, 6), (6, 8), and the same V-columns for the zero columns (Lemma 2.2),
but a different R: each pivot row is zero everywhere to the right of its pivot.

svg.text: for j′ > j with R[i, j′] ≠ 0: ▷ look ahead
▷ the whole pivot row to the right is zeroed,
▷ so every column is reduced when it is reached
